data.title: Australia Orders LNG Exporters Reserve Some Gas to Plug Shortages at Home — Update
data.description:
By Rhiannon Hoyle

Australia will require liquefied natural gas exporters to reserve up to a fifth of their shipments for the domestic market to help lower power bills for local households and businesses.

The law, approved early Friday, comes amid forecasts of supply shortfalls along the country's densely populated east coast--including Sydney and Melbourne--as traditional local gas fields deplete. The requirement takes effect Jan. 1, 2028, to align with industry contracting cycles, officials said.

"Australia has abundant gas resources and Australians should benefit from them," said Resources Minister Madeleine King. "This scheme will make more Australian gas available to our households and businesses, putting downward pressure on prices."

Australia is among the world's largest LNG exporters following significant investment by companies such as ConocoPhillips and Shell. The majority of Australian LNG is shipped to Japan, China and South Korea, with about three-quarters sold under long-term contracts.

The rule won't apply to producers in the state of Western Australia, which accounts for more than half the nation's LNG capacity and already has its own policy to reserve 15% of supply for the local market.

It comes amid a volatile year in global LNG markets, after disruptions to supplies from Qatar--another of the world's top exporters, along with the U.S.--sent prices sharply higher.

Energy producers criticized the new law, saying it threatens investment in more gas production.

"The reservation scheme will destroy investment signals for new gas supply, crowd out domestic-focused producers, and ultimately increase the risk of higher prices and less reliable energy for Australian households, manufacturers and businesses," said Samantha McCulloch, chief executive of Australian Energy Producers, an industry group.

Australia's Business Council, which says it represents the nation's largest employers and supports gas reservation, also raised some concerns about how the obligation will work and called for a review once it starts, to ensure the policy is working as intended.

"Ultimately, we can't know for certain how this policy will operate in practice until we put it to work, and the test for success will be whether it supports investment in new supply, puts downward pressure on energy costs and maintains our reputation as a reliable trading partner," Business Council Chief Executive Bran Black said.

Write to Rhiannon Hoyle at rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com

data.title: Consumer earnings growth to hinge on margin recovery; Titan, Marico top picks: Motilal Oswal
data.description:
Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services expects the next phase of consumer sector earnings to rely on profitability rather than topline expansion. "Overall, our assessment is that the next leg of earnings growth potentially will be driven by margins recovery and not much by revenue acceleration, which has already happened," he stated.

Companies under the brokerage's consumer coverage reported a 15% aggregate revenue growth in the July-September quarter of 2026 (Q2FY27), but elevated input costs restricted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) growth to just 7%.

Rural consumption is now outperforming urban markets, with discretionary segments such as quick-service restaurants (QSRs) and premium liquor showing signs of revival.

Moderating commodity prices and calibrated price hikes are expected to support a gradual margin recovery in the second half of 2026-27 (FY27), with a significant portion of that benefit materialising in the January-March quarter of 2027 (Q4FY27).

Risks to this outlook include a weak monsoon, fading goods and services tax (GST) benefits, and macroeconomic inflation. Within the sector, Motilal Oswal prefers Titan Company as a steady compounder and Radico Khaitan as a premiumisation play.

Marico is another top pick, benefiting from a gross margin expansion of nearly 600 basis points due to soft copra prices, alongside diversification into foods and premium products.

Shifting to the information technology (IT) sector, the brokerage maintains a neutral broader stance due to persistent headwinds, though specific pockets offer value. Largecap players like Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Infosys continue to face margin pressures, with the latter lowering its growth guidance. However, order flows and execution are strengthening at HCLTech and Tech Mahindra, aided by a management change at the latter.

"With a lot of these global AI trade unwinding and the Indian IT's AI play, which is what the valuation got derated in the last one-one-and-a-half years, I think a lot of new flows and market interest will now come back to IT," Khemka noted. Tier-two firms Coforge, Persistent Systems, and Mphasis are also favoured for their strong deal wins, improving margins, and comfortable valuations.

Addressing Urban Company's entry into the residential air conditioning market, the move from an asset-light to an asset-heavy model is viewed as a natural progression that leverages the firm's existing service and distribution strength, similar to the Eureka Forbes model. To capture market share in a highly competitive space, the company is offering a five-year service guarantee, though discounting practices and the evolving business model will require monitoring.

Watch the full conversation here

The core home services business continues to benefit from strong customer acquisition. While the InstaHelp segment of Urban Company. recently faced concerns over high competition and losses, it is now gaining market share and is expected to perform significantly better once it turns profitable.

data.title: Thailand's Bangchak buys prompt diesel following Bangkok refinery fire, sources say
data.description:
Thailand's Bangchak Corp has bought prompt 10-ppm sulphur diesel for early December delivery after a fire forced the shutdown of its Phra Khanong oil refinery in Bangkok, according to two people with knowledge of the matter.

Here are further details:

  • The refiner bought some volumes at premiums of slightly more than $3 a barrel above benchmark Singapore 10-ppm gasoil prices on a free-on-board basis, the people said

  • Given the short delivery window, the cargo was likely to be loaded in Southeast Asia

  • The exact volume purchased could not be confirmed

  • Bangchak had initially sought up to 40,000 metric tons of the industrial and transport fuel on November 26 for delivery aboard short-range tankers, one of the people said

  • The fire broke out at the 120,000-barrel-per-day refinery on the afternoon of November 26. The company attributed it to an incident at the refiner's hydrocracking unit

  • The company did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on the purchase

data.title: Malaysian palm oil rises on Dalian strength, eyes weekly gain
data.description:
By Dewi Kurniawati

Malaysian palm oil futures rose on Friday, supported by gains in rival vegetable oils and a technical rebound from recent lows, with the benchmark contract on track for a weekly gain.

The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange added 41 ringgit, or 0.96%, to 4,333 ringgit ($1,052.98) a metric ton during by the midday break.

The futures have booked a 2.75% weekly gain so far.

"The futures' increase is mainly driven by technical rebound after the recent double bottom while tracking Dalian performance," a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said.

Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market

Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 1.19%, while its palm oil contract added 1.72%. The Chicago Board of Trade (BOCv1) is on a modified Thanksgiving holiday schedule, with an early close on Friday.

State export monitoring firm Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia (DSI) is still evaluating the final fee it will charge for its services, the company's chief executive said on Friday.

Palm oil group GAPKI said on Thursday, DSI has proposed a service fee of 0.5% of the value of palm oil exports.

Crude palm oil prices are expected to stay above 4,100 ringgit per metric ton in December, as supply risks emerge heading into 2027, the Malaysian Palm Oil Council said on Wednesday.

Exports of Malaysian palm oil products for November 1 to 25 fell 9.3% from October 1 to 25, independent inspection company AmSpec Agri Malaysiasaid, while cargo surveyor Intertek Testing Services estimated a 4% drop.

The ringgit MYR=, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.05% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.

Palm oil may rise to 4,372 ringgit per metric ton, the peak of a wave b, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.

($1 = 4.1150 ringgit)

data.title: Oil on track to snap 3-week losing streak over supply fears
data.description:
Key points:
  • Attack on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery halts some operations
  • OPEC+ likely to roll over oil output targets for Q1
  • Russian oil refinery in Krasnodar region on fire after drone attack

Oil prices rose slightly on Friday and are on track to snap a three-week losing streak as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil supply from the conflict-hit Middle East.

Brent crude futures rose 4 cents to $96.61 a barrel by 0450 GMT, after gaining nearly $2 on Thursday to settle at their highest since November 6.

US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were at $85.78 a barrel, up $2.10, or 2.5%, from their close on Wednesday. There was no settlement for WTI on Thursday due to the Thanksgiving holiday in the US.

"We think Brent can still push above USD100/bbl without another major escalation in the Middle East, but that increasingly requires evidence of constrained deliverable supply," ANZ analysts Brian Martin and Daniel Hynes said in a note.

Prices slipped in previous weeks on relief that US President Donald Trump did not step up military action on Iran after the midterm elections. However, Iran has continued to attack ships transiting the Hormuz strait, disrupting oil exports, while Yemeni Houthis have struck Saudi infrastructure.

"Recovering Gulf exports and easing geopolitical risk support lower oil prices in 2027. However, depleted inventories, persistent shipping risks and slow refinery repairs leave the market exposed," OCBC analyst Sim Moh Siong said in a note.

Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery temporarily halted some operations after a projectile struck the facility on Thursday, killing a Nepalese worker and wounding several others, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said in a statement.

The strike was the Houthis' latest blow against key Saudi facilities, a day after the group claimed attacks on Ras Tanura, the kingdom's largest refinery and a major crude export hub, and the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, amid escalating hostilities between the two sides.

Given the disruption from the Iran war, OPEC+ is likely to maintain its oil output targets for at least the first quarter of 2027 at a meeting on Sunday, two sources said.

Meanwhile, Ukraine has intensified drone attacks on Russian oil refineries since the end of October, with the latest incident causing a fire at the Slavyansk ECO refinery in Russia's southern Krasnodar region.

Separately, fires disrupted activity at Thailand's Bangchak refinery and Venezuela's Amuay refinery on Thursday.

data.title: China stocks edge up as industrial profit growth buoys sentiment; tech leads gains
data.description:
By Summer Zhen

China and Hong Kong stocks rose on Friday as robust industrial profit growth buoyed market sentiment, with AI and chipmaking shares leading the advance.

** China's blue-chip CSI300 Index climbed 0.2% by the lunch break, while the Shanghai Composite Index gained 0.3%.

** Hong Kong's benchmark Hang Seng (.HIS) index was up 0.9%.

** Profit growth at China's industrial firms accelerated in October to the fastest in five months, mainly driven by AI-related industries and upstream sectors, although broader economic momentum remained subdued.

** Industrial figures gave market confidence a modest lift as stocks rebounded from a steep recent selloff, while investors assessed renewed tariff risks.

** In mainland A-shares, semiconductor materials and equipment stocks (.CSI931743) rallied as much as 8%, while cloud computing (.CSI931469) jumped 6% as investors bought the dip and bet on domestic tech substitution.

** In Hong Kong, Hang Seng Tech gained more than 3% by midday, with AI startup Minimax and Shanghai Iluvatar CoreX Semiconductor bouncing over 10% each.

** In contrast, the aviation and energy sectors were among the biggest underperformers.

** US President Donald Trump proposed new maximum tariff rates of 20% to 40% on Wednesday on goods from 14 major trading partners including China, Japan ​and the European Union.

** However, BofA Securities analysts believe the move is unlikely to reignite trade tensions.

** "The headline overstates the incremental tariff increase, and the proposal remains broadly consistent with the existing US-China trade framework," the bank said.

** The smaller Shenzhen index was up 2.32%, the start-up board ChiNext Composite index was higher by 3.79% and Shanghai's tech-focused STAR50 index was up 4.43%​.

data.title: ReFuels Q2 2027: CNG Fuels nearly doubles H1 adjusted EBITDA, expects full-year earnings at upper end of guidance
data.description:
27 November 2026: ReFuels N.V. (ticker: REFL) ("ReFuels"), one of Europe's leading suppliers of renewable biomethane (Bio-CNG) for the decarbonisation of heavy goods vehicles, today releases its interim report for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 for July–September 2026.

Highlights:

  • H1 2027 adj. EBITDA increased 98% to GBP 8.9 million, compared to H1 2026, with a third consecutive quarter of positive station network contribution
  • CNG Fuels FY 2027 adj. EBITDA guidance of GBP 16–20 million expected at the upper end of the range
  • Nearly 200 6x2 Bio-CNG trucks operating across 25 fleets, supporting broader adoption among UK heavy-duty operators
  • EU to review heavy-duty vehicle CO₂ standards, potentially paving the way for greater recognition of renewable fuels
  • Opened 17th high-capacity station, with two more under construction and MRS fleet expected to grow from 11 to 14 units
  • Continued network expansion supports CNG Fuels’ target of more than 8,000 Bio-CNG HGVs on UK roads by 2030

Philip Fjeld, CEO and co-founder of ReFuels, said:

“The case for Bio-CNG remains compelling, with significantly lower emissions, greater security of supply and a proven long-term fuel cost advantage over diesel. Adoption continues to broaden, with nearly 200 of the larger 6x2 trucks now on the road and more coming soon. Together with our station build-out, this will enable future growth. CNG Fuels delivered its third consecutive quarter of positive station network contribution, reflecting improving economies of scale, alongside strong certificate earnings. We now expect FY2027 adjusted EBITDA to be at the upper end of our guidance range of GBP 16–20 million.”

The second quarter 2027 interim report and presentation are attached and available at: https://refuels.com/investor-relations/

ReFuels will present the second quarter 2027 results today at 10:00 CET. The webcast will be hosted by CEO Philip Fjeld and CFO Baden Gowrie-Smith. Please register for the presentation via the following link: https://bit.ly/4AMuOsP

ReFuels is decarbonising Europe's truck fleet through its 40% ownership of CNG Fuels – a fully integrated clean fuel infrastructure platform combining sourcing of renewable biomethane (Bio-CNG), Renewable Transport Fuel Certificates (RTFCs), and ownership and operation of the UK's largest clean fuel station network. data.title: Energy Holdings Q3 2026: Strong performance, backlog growth and strategic progress
data.description:
Limassol, Cyprus - November 27, 2026: SED Energy Holdings Plc ("Energy Holdings") delivered continued positive financial and operational development in the third quarter of 2026, driven by a fully utilized Energy Drilling fleet, partly offset by lower activity in SeaBird Exploration. During the quarter, Energy Holdings and Ventura Offshore Holding Ltd. signed a letter of intent to combine, creating a more diversified platform with greater scale and a stronger capital markets profile. Closing of the proposed combination is expected during the first quarter of 2027.

“Energy Holdings delivered a solid third quarter, with important progress on both contracts and strategic initiatives. New contract awards across both businesses strengthen contract coverage into 2027, and the proposed combination with Ventura Offshore remains on track for closing in the first quarter,” said Kurt M. Waldeland, CEO.

Distributions for the second half of 2026 have been deferred until after completion of the proposed combination. This is a timing consequence of the transaction agreements, which do not permit distributions to shareholders before closing. Energy Holdings remains fully committed to distributing available excess liquidity to shareholders and will resume distributions once the transaction completes. On a standalone basis, Energy Holdings maintains its full-year distribution guidance of USD 90-110 million and will provide an update on the deferred amount at closing.

“Looking ahead, we are seeing encouraging signs that activity in our markets is improving. Underlying demand for tender-assist drilling in Southeast Asia remains strong, while tendering activity and visibility in marine seismic are improving. We expect to continue adding to our backlog in the coming months, and remain focused on converting this activity into high utilization, strong cash generation and sustainable shareholder returns,” Waldeland continued.

Q3 2026 highlights:

  • Revenue of USD 66.4 million and EBITDA of USD 37.0 million, with last twelve months EBITDA of USD 149 million, supported by continued high activity in Energy Drilling.
  • Net cash flow from operating activities amounted to USD 107.0 million in the first nine months of 2026.
  • Net interest-bearing debt1 was USD 22.7 million at quarter-end, corresponding to 0.2x LTM adjusted EBITDA.
  • Energy Drilling delivered strong performance with economic utilization of 99%. SeaBird completed the five-year classing of Fulmar Explorer and mobilized Eagle Explorer, resulting in lower utilization in the period.
  • After quarter-end, Energy Drilling secured contracts for the T-16 and SeaBird secured a new contract for Fulmar Explorer starting in late 2026.
  • Firm revenue backlog was USD 367 million, including contracts awarded after quarter-end.
  • Due to transaction-related restrictions associated with the contemplated combination with Ventura Offshore, shareholder distributions for the second half of 2026 will be announced after completion of the transaction.
  • Standalone full-year distribution guidance of USD 90–110 million reiterated, of which USD 50 million has been declared for the first half of 2026.

Third quarter 2026 presentation

The third quarter 2026 materials are enclosed and available on the company's website: www.energyholdings.cy/investors/financial-reports/.

Energy Holdings will present its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 in a live audio webcast today at 10:00 CET, hosted by Kurt M. Waldeland, Chief Executive Officer, Sveinung Alvestad, Chief Financial Officer, and Viggo Pedersen, Chief Investment Officer.

The presentation will be followed by a Q&A session and questions may be submitted in writing at any time during the event. A recording of the webcast will be made available on the company's website after the live event has been concluded.
